title: stage-needs
intention: Attach dependencies to the WORKFLOW STAGE that needs them, not to the ticket as a whole — and make the act of LOOKING compile back into the ticket. A stage declares what it needs; whenever anyone checks the world, the finding is stamped onto that need with WHAT, WHEN and HOW MEASURED. Retire the ad-hoc `waits_on` field once its content is migrated.
why: Two failures measured on 2026-07-26, and they have one fix. FIRST: dependency had no honest representation. `waits_on` is authored by hand on 6 of 10 staged tickets, is in NO node-class schema, is PROSE (voyage.py:75 already says so: 'the ticket's prose waits_on is narrative, not a clean party to render'), is consumed by nothing, and is DROPPED at berthing — zero of 25 berthed charters carry it. So the dependency record is destroyed by the act of finishing. SECOND: the record kept disagreeing with the world — 'awaiting Akien's signature' when there was nowhere to sign; 'no inference host' with ollama serving on :11434 for four days. Akien's shape fixes both: needs are declared per-stage (intrinsic, stable), and the OBSERVATION is compiled in even when nobody picks the ticket up — so going and looking is what keeps the record honest, and the two can no longer drift.
traces_to: Law 1 — 'the fact that we went and looked gets compiled into the ticket' IS Law 1: the answered question becomes structure, so the next mind reads the measurement instead of repeating it.
Law 3 — a need's status is a MEASUREMENT with a time and a method, not an assertion. A bare [DONE] is an unmeasured claim wearing a checkmark.
Law 4 — the shape is enforced by the schema and the write door, not by anyone remembering to update prose.
Law 7 — a stale mark must be VISIBLE as stale; collapsing 'measured three weeks ago' into 'done' is a record of truth losing information.

proves_green.prove_gate: proof gate — the tester runs the node's proof and emits a VALIDATION.
proves_green.durability_gate: not done until tested AND durably committed (git).

falsifier.proves_red: A mark lacking WHEN or HOW MEASURED must be REFUSED at the write door — a bare [DONE] cannot be written. Staleness must be QUERYABLE: given a ticket, the system reports the age of each mark, so 'this DONE is 21 days old' is a fact on the surface rather than an invisible assumption. And the shape must carry a REAL case end-to-end: the librarian's BUILD stage needs {inference host, embeddings generator, store design}; the host mark must record today's measurement (ollama :11434, three models, embed 768d, 2026-07-26) and the other two must sit unmarked. A hollow build — a checkbox with no timestamp, or a needs list nothing can query — fails every clause.
falsifier.horizon: Re-read when the FIRST ticket is picked up under this shape. The open question the gate surfaced: does a mark ever EXPIRE by itself (a host can go down after being marked DONE), or is age always reported and judged by the reader? Deliberately NOT guessed — no expiry has been measured as needed, and inventing a TTL ahead of evidence is the same error as guessing a chatter-damping width. Filed, not built.
